overview.text: This RFP invites bids from contractors for the '2nd Call' of a Percentage Rate Contract to execute balance work rectifying damages to bituminous pavement and roadside drains for laying PHED pipelines on NH-510 in Sikkim. The project, located at Package-III (KM 32.500 to 33.600), is part of the 'Construction of 2-lane specification road with paved shoulder including Tunnel' under SARDP-NE Phase-A.

issuing_organization: National Highways & Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited (NHIDCL)

scope.text: Scope includes balance work for rectification of damages to bituminous pavement and roadside drains, laying PHED pipelines, and general road maintenance activities.
Contractor must demonstrate availability of key equipment including Tipper/Dumper Truck (1 unit), Back hoe loader (1 unit), and Tandem Roller (8-10 Ton) (1 unit).
Bidder must provide Key Personnel including a Project Manager with B.E./B.Tech/AMIE in Civil Engineering and minimum 5 years of experience.
Contractor is required to maintain road assets, execute maintenance works, and comply with Road Maintenance Standards and Specifications.

key_requirements.text: Bidder must submit financial reports for the last three years certified by a Chartered Accountant and proof of turnover.
Bidders must furnish an irrevocable, unconditional e-Bank Guarantee from a Scheduled Commercial Bank with net worth not less than Rs. 500 crore.
Performance Security must be an unconditional e-Bank Guarantee for 5% of the Bid Price, valid until 60 days after the Defect Liability Period.
Contractor must deploy technical personnel named in Contract Data within 15 days of notice to proceed; failure incurs penalties.

eligibility.text: Bidder must have achieved a minimum average annual financial turnover (civil engineering construction/maintenance) equal to the amount indicated in NIT for the last three years.
Bidder must satisfactorily complete similar works on National/State Highways during the last five years as prime contractor or JV partner (not less than 90% of contract value).
Bidder must have available bid capacity greater than the total estimated value put to tender, calculated using the formula: (A* N* 2.5 - B).

important_dates.text: Bid Due Date is 14.04.2026 at 16:00 Hrs for physical document submission.
Bids must remain valid for a period of 120 days after the deadline date for bid submission.
Performance Security must be furnished within 10 days of receipt of Letter of Acceptance.

commercial_requirements.text: Contract is awarded on a Percentage Rate Contract Basis; rates and prices are fixed for the duration of the Contract and not subject to adjustment.
Payment basis relies on actual quantities of work carried out valued at tendered rates along with any accepted/awarded tender premium.
Performance-based activities are indexed on a performance scale of 100 marks; payment is not entitled if average performance is rated less than 80%.

project_duration.text: Intended Completion Date may be revised only by the Engineer by issuing an Extension of Time after approval from the Employer.
The Contractor shall not sub-contract the whole of Works.
If any defect exceeds the permissible tolerance, it shall be treated as 'non-compliance'.
The security deposit/retention money is retained until Completion of the whole Works and release depends on certification of Defects Liability Period completion.
The Performance Security must be valid until a date 60 days after the expiry of the Defects Liability Period (accounting for additional months for BG verification/signing/start).

The intended completion date is within 3 months from the start date (derived as 1 month in Contract Data but referenced as Clauses 1.1, 17 & 26 suggesting standard conditions). *Correction based on explicit text on Page 67: The intended completion date for whole of work is 01 month from start date.*
The start date shall be within 15 days after the date of issue of the Notice to proceed.

important_conditions.text: Confidentiality obligations apply; bid evaluation results and award decisions shall not be disclosed until the award is announced.
Subcontracting is not allowed (limit is Nil); Contractor remains fully liable for all acts, defaults, and neglects of sub-contractors.
Contractor must comply with labour laws including the Child Labour (Prohibition & Regulation) Act, 1986 and Apprentices Act, 1961.
